idiom_name: record with init-only properties + with-expressions (ImmutableArray for collections)
implementation_notes: The language supplies the structure: a positional record class declares init-only properties that can be set only while constructing, generates value equality and ToString, and a with-expression performs non-destructive mutation by copying the instance and overriding selected members. The state is still only shallowly immutable, so a record that holds a List<T> must copy it (an ImmutableArray<T>, or an explicit defensive copy in the constructor) instead of storing the caller's object. Use the classic readonly-field class where the type must join a class hierarchy, where value equality is wrong for the type, or where an older language version is required.
pitfalls: Records are only shallowly immutable: an init-only property can still point at a mutable List<T> and the compiler never inserts a defensive copy - store ImmutableArray<T> or copy in the compact constructor.
The generated value equality uses every positional member, so a record holding a mutable component changes hash when that component changes; do not use such a record as a dictionary key.
record struct is not immutable by default - its positional properties are read-write; the immutable value-type form is readonly record struct.

variants.name: private readonly fields with get-only properties
variants.idiom_name: sealed class with private readonly fields and get-only properties
variants.implementation_notes: The classic form works on every C# version: a sealed class or readonly struct keeps its state in readonly fields assigned in the constructor, exposes get-only properties, and expresses updates as methods that return a new instance. It preserves ordinary class identity and inheritance relationships and is the right choice when the type must derive from another class or when value equality is not wanted.
pitfalls: readonly on a reference field protects the reference, not the object: a readonly List<T> field is still mutable through its own methods, which is why CA2104 warns about externally visible read-only mutable reference types.
A readonly struct is copied on every assignment and boxes when converted to an interface; keep such types small and do not let a mutable static field quietly become part of their state.
